name: Skill Orb
Source: Dropped by monsters, found in dungeons, awarded by gods
Effect: Teaches one random skill of common or uncommon tier when activated
Usage: Crush in hand to absorb knowledge
Description: A translucent crystal orb swirling with faint golden light. When crushed, the knowledge of a single skill floods into the user's mind. The skill gained depends on the orb's origin.

name: Greater Skill Orb
Source: Boss monsters, high-level dungeons, legendary chests
Effect: Teaches one random skill of rare or fable tier when activated
Usage: Crush in hand to absorb knowledge
Description: A brilliant orb of condensed knowledge, pulsing with inner light. Warriors and mages alike seek these for the rare techniques sealed within.

name: Skill Reset Orb
Source: Dungeon bosses, rare events, purchased from roaming merchants
Effect: Resets all learned skills to their base state, refunding all skill XP
Usage: Crush in hand to trigger skill redistribution
Description: A deep blue orb crackling with temporal energy. Using it rewinds your skill progression, allowing complete re-specialization.

name: Monster Core (Feral)
Source: Looted from low-level monsters and wild beasts
Effect: Used to enchant low-tier gear, craft basic potions, or fuel minor magic items
Usage: Crushed for essence or socketed into equipment
Description: A rough, pulsing shard of raw monster essence. The chaotic energy inside can be harnessed by alchemists and enchanters for basic enhancements.

name: Monster Core (Arcane)
Source: Looted from magical beasts, elementals, and spellcasting monsters
Effect: Powers magic item crafting, enchantment rituals, and high-tier potions
Usage: Crushed for essence or consumed in rituals
Description: A smooth crystalline core humming with stored arcane energy. Wizards pay handsomely for these to fuel their most ambitious enchantments.

name: Monster Core (Dragon)
Source: Extracted from adult or ancient dragons
Effect: Used to craft legendary weapons, dragon-scale armor, and world-class artifacts
Usage: Consumed in legendary crafting rituals
Description: A fist-sized gem of immense power, radiating the primal fury of a dragon. Only master smiths and archmages dare work with such volatile energy.

name: Guild Card (Bronze)
Source: Issued by any Adventurer's Guild upon registration
Effect: Identifies the bearer as a registered adventurer. Tracks completed quests and rank progression.
Usage: Carried on person. Presented for guild services.
Description: A stamped metal card bearing the guild's insignia and your name. At bronze rank, it grants access to basic quest boards and guild facilities.

name: Guild Card (Silver)
Source: Promotion from Bronze after completing 20+ quests
Effect: Grants access to advanced quests, guild loans, and restricted shop items
Usage: Carried on person. Presented for guild services.
Description: An elegant silver-plated card with engraved filigree. At silver rank, merchants offer discounts and guild banks extend credit.

name: Guild Card (Gold)
Source: Promotion from Silver after completing 50+ quests and a rank-up trial
Effect: Grants VIP access to all guild services, priority quest selection, and royal audience privileges
Usage: Carried on person. Presented for guild services.
Description: A gleaming gold card inlaid with a flawless gem. Gold-rank adventurers are treated as nobility in most towns and can request direct audiences with regional lords.

name: Teleportation Crystal
Source: Enchanted by mages, found in ancient ruins, sold at magic shops
Effect: Teleports the user to the last city or sanctuary they registered at
Usage: Crush or activate verbally to trigger teleportation
Description: A clear crystal with a swirling vortex trapped inside. When activated, it folds space and instantly transports the user to a bound location. Single-use.

name: Recall Crystal
Source: Sold at general stores, crafted by apprentice mages
Effect: Returns the user to their spawn point or home location
Usage: Crush to activate recall
Description: A small gray crystal linked to the world's leylines. A cheap and reliable way to return home from an adventure gone wrong.

name: Binding Crystal
Source: Crafted by archmages, found in mage tower vaults
Effect: Sets a custom teleportation anchor point at current location
Usage: Activate at the desired location to bind it. Then use a Teleportation Crystal to return.
Description: A violet crystal that can etch a permanent spatial anchor into the fabric of reality. Once bound, any Teleportation Crystal will bring you back to this exact spot.

name: Phoenix Down
Source: Grown in phoenix nesting grounds, rare alchemical creation
Effect: Revives a fallen ally with 25% HP. Only works on the recently fallen.
Usage: Wave over the fallen companion's body
Description: A single crimson feather from a phoenix, still warm to the touch. When brushed across a fallen comrade, the spark of life rekindles in their chest.

name: Revival Crystal
Source: Blessed by high priests, found in sacred tombs, granted by deities
Effect: Fully revives a fallen ally with all HP and MP restored. Cures all status effects.
Usage: Hold over the fallen and channel mana
Description: A tear-shaped diamond suffused with holy light. Priests spend years blessing these crystals. One touch reverses death itself.

name: Identification Crystal
Source: Crafted by appraisers, sold at magic item shops
Effect: Identifies the magical properties of one unknown item
Usage: Tap against the unidentified item
Description: A small prismatic crystal that resonates with enchantments. Tap it against any unidentified item to reveal its magical properties, rarity, and origin.

name: Status Plate (HP/MP)
Source: Crafted by enchanters, sold at guild supply shops
Effect: Displays the user's current HP, MP, and status effects in a floating window
Usage: Attach to equipment or wear as an accessory
Description: A small glass plate etched with runes that project a translucent status window. Popular among adventurers who prefer numbers over feelings to know when they're about to die.

name: Blessing Amulet of the Goddess
Source: Granted by a divine being upon arrival to the new world, or found in a hidden temple
Effect: Grants +1 to all stats, provides slow HP regeneration, and warns of imminent deadly danger
Usage: Wear around neck
Description: A silver amulet bearing the emblem of a forgotten goddess. Often the first gift an isekai protagonist receives. Its protective aura has saved countless lives.

name: Magic Bag of Holding (Portable Crafting)
Source: Crafted by master enchanters, dropped by mimic bosses
Effect: Contains a small pocket dimension with a workbench and basic tools. Items stored inside are weightless.
Usage: Reach inside to access the crafting space and storage
Description: A deceptively small bag that opens into a fully equipped workshop. Everything you need for field repairs, potion brewing, and gear upgrades fits inside.

name: Cheat Skill Tome
Source: Appears in the protagonist's inventory upon arrival in the new world
Effect: Grants a unique, world-breaking skill (Appraisal, Limit Break, All Crafting Max, etc.)
Usage: Open and read to instantly learn the contained skill
Description: A tome that appears only for those chosen by fate. The skill within is unique and cannot be learned through normal means. The contents adapt to the reader's needs.

name: Rasengan Orb
Source: Found in a sealed scroll within a hidden hot spring cave, guarded by a pervy sage
Effect: When activated, creates a spiraling sphere of chakra/energy that deals massive piercing damage and launches enemies backward
Usage: Hold in palm and focus mana to form the spinning energy sphere
Description: A perfectly spherical crystal with a miniature hurricane trapped inside. A pervy old sage once said: 'The secret is in the spin.' The orb trembles with barely contained rotational force.

name: Instant Death Spell Scroll (One-Time)
Source: Sealed within a magic vault, dropped by a lich, reward for defeating a demon lord general
Effect: Instantly kills any non-boss, non-immortal enemy below level 50. No save, no resist.
Usage: Read aloud to cast. Scroll crumbles to ash after use.
Description: A scroll bound in black leather with a skull-shaped seal. The spell written inside bypasses all defenses and simply ends the target's existence. One use only.

name: Bento of the Hero's Journey
Source: Prepared by a childhood friend, mysterious wandering chef, or doting mother figure
Effect: Fully restores HP, MP, and stamina. Removes all minor status ailments. Provides +10% EXP for 1 hour.
Usage: Eat during a short rest
Description: A lovingly packed wooden box containing rice, grilled fish, pickled vegetables, and a small octopus-shaped sausage. The taste of home in any world.

name: Demon Lord's Seal (Cursed Armament)
Source: Sealed beneath the royal castle, bestowed by the hero's lineage, dropped by the Demon Lord
Effect: Deals 5x damage to demon-kind. Slowly drains HP while drawn. Can seal a demon's powers on critical hit.
Usage: Wield as a sword or seal as a talisman
Description: A jet-black blade that drinks light. Forged from the core of a fallen star and sealed for centuries. The demon lords fear this weapon above all others.

name: Auto-Translate Earring
Source: Sold at guild shops, crafted by translation mages, standard isekai welcome kit item
Effect: Automatically translates all written and spoken languages into the wearer's native tongue
Usage: Wear as an earring or amulet
Description: A simple bronze earring enchanted with universal translation magic. Why every isekai protagonist encounters one immediately upon arrival remains a cosmic mystery.

name: Gacha Ticket (Bronze)
Source: Daily login rewards, quest completion bonuses, purchased at general stores
Effect: Pulls one random item from the Common-Uncommon pool
Usage: Present at any gacha machine or summoning shrine
Description: A paper ticket stamped with a cheap wax seal. The thrill of gambling without the financial ruin — mostly common items, but hey, someone has to get the rare.

name: Gacha Ticket (Gold)
Source: Weekly quest rewards, boss drops, real-money microtransactions
Effect: Pulls one random item from the Rare-Fable pool
Usage: Present at any gacha machine or summoning shrine
Description: A gilded ticket with a holographic emblem. The drop rates are still terrible but the dopamine hit is legendary.

name: One-Hit-Kill Dagger (Over-levelled Starter Weapon)
Source: Appears in protagonist's inventory as a 'worthless' starter weapon that turns out to be endgame material
Effect: Deals (current enemy HP) damage to any non-boss enemy. Ignores all armor and defenses. Absolutely useless against bosses — they just take 1 damage.
Usage: Stab the enemy. It dies. (Unless it's a boss.)
Description: A dull, unassuming iron dagger that any vendor would appraise at 3 gold. The gods have a sick sense of humor. Somehow, this thing bypasses the concept of 'health bar' entirely.

name: Save Point Crystal (Checkpoint)
Source: Embedded in ancient dungeons, protected by floor guardians
Effect: Creates a save point. If the party wipes, they respawn here with 50% HP/MP. Boss room save points deactivate after boss defeat.
Usage: Touch to set checkpoint
Description: A crystalline obelisk pulsing with a gentle blue light. Touching it imprints your soul on this moment in time. Death is no longer the end — it's just a setback.

name: Harem Protection Pendant
Source: Crafted by a lonely archmage, dropped by a yandere boss
Effect: Passively charms non-hostile NPCs within 10m. +5 to all social skill checks. WARNING: May attract unwanted romantic attention.
Usage: Wear around neck at all times
Description: A heart-shaped pendant set with a pink gem. Every protagonist who wears one mysteriously finds themselves surrounded by adoring companions of all genders and species. Coincidence? Probably not.

name: Level-Up Crystal (Instant Growth)
Source: Dropped by mini-bosses, purchased from the System Shop, seasonal event rewards
Effect: Immediately grants one level-up. Cannot be used past level 50.
Usage: Crush to absorb XP
Description: A shimmering prism that contains a concentrated burst of experience energy. Adventurers joke that these are how the rich buy their levels, but nobody refuses one.
